37	=== 36
38	R1 02: Alchemy stack and per-PR preview stages [CLOSED]
39	Slice 2 of [Release 1: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/34).
40	
41	## Goal
42	The deployable walking skeleton: both Workers, the Organization Durable Object, D1, and Queues, deployed to a fresh stage for every PR and destroyed when the PR closes.
43	
44	## Acceptance criteria
45	- An Alchemy v2 stack in `infra` with:
46	  - the Main Worker (`app.` host; serves the API and static assets from `apps/web`);
47	  - the Submission Worker (`submit.` host; `observability.enabled=false`, logs/traces off, `logpush=false`, no tail consumers);
48	  - the Organization DO (SQLite, migrations);
49	  - a D1 database (empty migration);
50	  - a Queue, a dead-letter queue, and a consumer for both.
51	- PR stages deploy as `pr-<n>` on `pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app` and `pr-<n>.submit.surveybeat.app`, from GitHub Actions with a Cloudflare API token secret and the Cloudflare state store. Closing the PR destroys the stage.
52	- One endpoint runs end to end: create an Organization record in its DO, then read it back through domain → api → adapter.
53	- **Deployed-settings read-back:** a post-deploy step reads each Worker's observability settings from the Cloudflare API and fails if any Submission Worker field that should be off is on, including `logs.invocation_logs` and `persist`. The spike found Alchemy leaves these on.

80	R1 03: Sign-in with AuthKit and Organization creation [CLOSED]
81	Slice 3 of [Release 1: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/34).
82	
83	## Goal
84	People sign in with WorkOS AuthKit. Allowlisted users can create an Organization, and everyone else is linked to the Person a Lead created for them.
85	
86	## Acceptance criteria
87	- AuthKit hosted UI with the six-digit email code, Google, and Microsoft. The Main Worker handles the OAuth callback, a sealed session cookie, refresh, and logout, using `@workos-inc/node`'s workerd build (see `docs/research/workos-authkit-workers.md`).
88	- **Per-request session check:** local JWT verification plus our own deny check (revoked session, Person removed, Membership ended). Access token lifetime is about 5 minutes.
89	- First sign-in with no matching Person: allowlisted email → "Create an Organization" (name only), idempotent per WorkOS user, and the creator becomes the Organization admin. Otherwise "You're not part of an Organization yet".
90	- Linking: a WorkOS user is linked to the Person with an exact **verified** email match. An unverified email never links. One verified email that matches Persons in several Organizations gets an Organization picker.
91	- The operator allowlist is configured per stage (a secret or config, never in code).
92	- D1 global index: WorkOS user → Persons, and email → Organizations for Persons not yet linked.
93	- Check whether WorkOS accepts wildcard redirect URIs for `pr-<n>` stages. If it doesn't, document the workaround.
94	
95	## Open choices

97	- Where the deny list lives (D1 or KV), given SPEC §6.2: "do not use KV for sessions that must be revoked at once".

110	The operator allowlist for creating an Organization is stored as the repo secret `ORG_CREATION_ALLOWLIST` (currently one address, the owner's). Read it per stage. Never hard-code it.
111	---
112	WorkOS is set up (2026-11-07):
113	- **Project:** `SurveyBeat` (`REDACTED`). **Staging** `REDACTED` (AuthKit domain `straightforward-mouse-82-staging.authkit.app`) is used for `pr-*` and personal stages. **Production** `REDACTED` is reserved for slice 15.
114	- **Repo secrets:** `WORKOS_API_KEY` (Staging secret key) and `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` (`REDACTED`), plus `ORG_CREATION_ALLOWLIST`.
115	- **Staging redirect URIs (wildcards are accepted):** `https://pr-*.app.surveybeat.app/auth/callback` (default), `https://*.chrisdoc.workers.dev/auth/callback`, `http://localhost:5173/auth/callback`. The callback path is therefore `/auth/callback`.

118	R1 04: People, Teams, roles, and Organization settings [CLOSED]
119	Slice 4 of [Release 1: implementation](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/34).
120	
121	## Goal
122	An Organization admin builds Teams, and a Lead adds members by email.
123	
124	## Acceptance criteria
125	- An Organization admin can create and rename Teams, assign and remove Leads, and add and remove People. Being an admin grants no access to any Team's Results (ADR 0003).
126	- A Lead (or an admin) adds members by email. This creates a Person (email only) and a Membership. It sends the "You've been added to <Team> by <Lead>" email through `EmailSender` (an in-memory adapter until slice 5).

128	  - the last Lead can't be removed;
129	  - removing a member ends their Membership on that date;
130	  - Person and history stay;
131	  - no Team nesting;
132	  - roles are lead and member only (viewer is modelled but unused).
133	- **The permission function** `(person, action, resource)` is defined in one place and tested as a table (SPEC §5.6).

148	- When a Person is removed, keep the D1 `person_index` in step and deactivate their WorkOS organization membership. The session check already denies removed Persons through the Organization DO, and Team Memberships should join that same DO check.

152	Follow-ups from the authorization review of PR #55 (no blockers found):
153	- **Q1, pending owner decision:** an admin adding themselves to a Team. Recommendation: allow it, but it must always show in the roster, and add a note to ADR 0003.

158	R1 05: Email sending: EmailSender, Queue consumer, send states, base template [CLOSED]

161	## Goal
162	Transactional email that is never sent twice and never fails silently.
163	
164	## Acceptance criteria
165	- An `EmailSender` domain interface with a Cloudflare Email Sending adapter on the new sending subdomain `notify.surveybeat.app`, provisioned with Alchemy `Cloudflare.Email.SendingSubdomain`. Don't touch the apex SPF/DMARC or the existing mail and SES records.
166	- The Queue consumer renders and sends. A send has the state `pending → sending → sent | failed(reason)`, with a lease. The consumer checks the state before sending. Clear provider rejections retry a few times and then become `failed`. **A lease that expires with no outcome becomes `failed: unknown` and is never resent automatically.**
167	- Bounce and complaint events update the send state, if Alchemy can express the event subscription. Otherwise record the workaround (see `docs/research/cloudflare-email-sending.md`).
168	- `packages/emails`: a React Email base layout (light and dark), the "You've been added" email, and the plain-text part.

208	R1 07: Round lifecycle engine in the Organization Durable Object [CLOSED]

210	
211	## Goal
212	Rounds run themselves: open per time zone, close once, compute, share, and create the next one, even if any job runs twice.
213	
214	## Acceptance criteria
215	- A schedule table plus one alarm set to the earliest due job. Each job is an idempotent DO method that runs in the same transaction as its state change.
216	- States: Scheduled → Open → Closed → Ready → Shared (Ready moves straight to Shared in R1), plus Cancelled.
217	- Open happens at the first member's local send. Eligible members are frozen then. **One close instant: the latest member's send time plus the window.**
218	- The next Round is always Scheduled. It is created with the Pulse and again at each open, keyed by Pulse and planned open date.
219	- Lead controls:
220	  - skip any of the next 8 weeks (skipping the Scheduled week cancels it);
221	  - pause cancels the Scheduled Round, and an Open Round runs to its end;
222	  - close early (uninvited members are never invited);
223	  - cancelling an Open Round deletes its Submissions and Participation records.
224	- A Scheduled Round picks up Pulse changes. An Open Round never changes.
225	- IANA time zones. Local times are converted to UTC when scheduled. In a daylight-saving gap the time moves forward; in an overlap the first occurrence wins.
226	- The daily Cron repairs missing alarms.
227	- The close job enqueues result computation. The compute itself is slice 11, so use a stub here.

Then their D1 `person_index` row is deleted, and their WorkOS organization membership is deactivated. A Person who never signed in has no WorkOS membership to touch. ## Decisions
- **The Template's Questions** (weekly team health, in order):
  1. Rating, workload: "How manageable was your workload this week?" (Not manageable … Very manageable, comment on)
  2. Rating, psychological safety: "How safe did you feel raising concerns or mistakes in the team?" (Not safe … Completely safe, comment on)
  3. Rating, clarity: "How clear were your priorities this week?" (Very unclear … Very clear)
  4. Rating, recognition: "How recognised did you feel for your work this week?" (Not at all … Very much)
  5. Single choice, workload: "What slowed you down most this week?" (Unclear goals / Waiting on others / Interruptions / Too much work / Nothing in particular)
  6. Long text, recognition: "Is there anything or anyone you would like to recognise from this week?"
- **Time estimate:** the sum of fixed seconds per type: rating 6 s, single choice 10 s, long text 30 s. The optional rating comment isn't counted, because most members skip it. The Template comes to 64 s.
- **Warnings, never refusals:**
  - more than 7 Questions;
  - more than 90 s;
  - the first Question is not a rating (no one-tap, ADR 0007);
  - the Team has fewer active Leads and members than N.
- **Hard rules (refusals):**
  - a Pulse keeps 1–20 Questions;
  - a Template Question appears at most once per Pulse;
  - a reorder must list each Question exactly once;
  - a Question with Answers can't be edited. Removing it is still allowed, and its version stays in the library.
- **Copying from the Template:** each Question added to a Pulse is a new library Question with version 1. An edit rewrites version 1 in place (allowed only without Answers) and detaches the Question from the Template, so the Template's original can be added again.
- **Settings:** a new Pulse defaults to Monday 09:00, 3 days, 1 reminder. The Team is fixed when the Pulse is created and is part of the URL. Lookups go through the Team, so a Pulse of another Team answers 404, and permission is checked before existence.

## Not verified
- The editor screens were built and type-checked but not clicked through: sign-in can't be automated locally. Please try them on the `pr-<n>` preview stage.

=== PR 59
R1 07: Round lifecycle engine
Closes #41. Part of #34.

### Changes
- **Rounds schema & domain models** (`packages/domain/src/rounds/`):
  - Defined schemas for `RoundId`, `JobId`, `RoundStatus`, `PlannedOpenDate`, `ScheduleJobType`, `ScheduleJobStatus`, `RoundQuestion`, `RoundMember`, `RoundSummary`, `RoundDetail`, `RoundList`.
  - Added errors: `RoundNotFound`, `RoundNotOpen`, `InvalidRoundState`, `WeekOutOfRange`.
  - Pure scheduling & time functions in `Lifecycle.ts`: `localToUtc` (Intl-based DST gap/overlap rules), `calculateRoundInstants`, `calculateReminders`, `nextWeekdayDate`, `nextEightWeeksCadenceDates`, `authorizeRoundAction`.
- **Durable Object database schema & repository** (`packages/cloudflare/`):
  - Added migration `0006_rounds.sql` adding `paused_at` to `pulse`, `pulse_skip`, `round` (unique on `(pulse_id, planned_open_date)`), `round_question`, `round_member`, `schedule_job`.
  - Implemented `SqlRounds.ts` for schedule jobs, round state transitions, member freezing, and pause/skip persistence with zero `any` and zero `as`.
- **Organization Durable Object lifecycle engine** (`packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.ts`):
  - Schedule table + ONE native DO alarm armed to `MIN(due_at)` of pending jobs via `repairAlarm()`.
  - Idempotent execution of `open`, `close`, and `compute` jobs (`runScheduleJob` / `runDueJobs`).
  - Scheduling next round upon pulse creation and round open.
  - Updating scheduled round on pulse edit (while open rounds remain unchanged).
  - Effective N calculation on close: `Math.max(org.minimumGroupSize, round.effectiveMinimumGroupSize ?? org.minimumGroupSize)` per ADR 0004.
  - Stub for slice 11 compute transitioning to Ready and immediately Shared in R1.
  - Clear seams left for invitations/sending (slice 08) and submissions/participations deletion on cancel (slice 09).
- **Lead controls API & Authorization**:
  - Authorized through permission table (`team.viewRounds`, `team.manageRounds` for `admin` and `lead`).
  - Endpoints in `rounds` group: `listRounds`, `getRound`, `skipWeek`, `unskipWeek`, `pausePulse`, `resumePulse`, `closeRoundEarly`, `cancelRound`.
  - Classified all 8 endpoints as `NoResultData` in `PrivacyRegistry.ts`.
- **Daily Cron Repair**:
  - Registered `Cloudflare.Workers.cron("0 0 * * *")` in `MainWorker.ts` repairing missing alarms across all organizations.
- **Tests**:
  - Domain tests in `Lifecycle.test.ts` with Effect `TestClock`: timezone spanning UTC-8 and UTC+9, DST spring-forward (gap) and fall-back (overlap), skip, pause, close, cancel, and scheduled round picking up pulse edits while open round does not.
  - DO adapter tests on local workerd in `Organization.test.ts`: verifying alarm always points to earliest due job, next round is never duplicated, and jobs run twice change nothing the second time.

### Decisions
- **Open and close instants**: Open happens at the earliest member's local send time across active memberships (frozen at open). There is one unified close instant: the latest member's send time plus the answer window.
- **DST handling**: `localToUtc` uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat` across all IANA time zones. Gaps (spring-forward) shift the local time forward by the gap duration, and overlaps (fall-back) take the first (earlier UTC) occurrence.
- **Schedule table & alarm**: Schedule table (`schedule_job`) tracks `due_at`, `type`, and `status`. A single alarm is armed via `repairAlarm()` to `MIN(due_at)` of pending jobs. Jobs run idempotently in SQLite transactions; repeating a completed job has no side effects.

=== PR 61
R1 08: Invitations, reminders, and failed-send view
Closes #42

### Summary
Members need their check-in invitation and reminders delivered on schedule to their inbox with single-tap rating links and easy delivery customization.

This PR implements the invitation and reminder engine for Release 1:
- Generates 128-bit base64url invitation tokens stored only as SHA-256 hashes in D1 `invitation_index` and Durable Object SQLite `invitation`.
- Dispatches transactional Invitation emails with anonymity statement, one-tap rating links (`https://app.surveybeat.app/a#t=<token>&v=<n>`), actions, and delivery preference links.
- Schedules reminders at member's local time zone, automatically skipping members who have answered, opted out, or when round close is within 2 hours.
- RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe endpoint (`/api/reminders/unsubscribe`) with DKIM-covered headers and no redirects.
- "Change when I get this" delivery preference page on Main Worker (`/delivery`) with client-side time zone detection.
- Failed invitations tracking in Round details and Lead resend command (`ResendInvitation`).
- GET/HEAD requests to `/delivery` and `/api/reminders/unsubscribe` perform strictly zero writes.

=== PR 62
R1 09: Submission Worker and anonymous Submission storage
Anonymous pulse survey answers must be stored in a way that prevents anyone—leads, admins, or database operators reading data at rest—from linking responses back to a person.

This PR implements Release 1 slice 09:
- **Submission Worker (\`packages/cloudflare/src/SubmissionWorker.ts\`)**:
  - \`POST /submit\`: Zero-side-effect canary route returning 202.
  - \`POST /exchange\`: Zero-side-effect token exchange resolving pulse name, anonymity statement, frozen questions, actions, close time, and round state.
  - \`POST /first-answer\` (and \`/answer\` with token): Atomically records \`participation\` (round and person, no timestamp) and \`submission\` in a single transaction in the Organization Durable Object. Stores edit key hash in D1 \`submission_index\`. Rejects duplicate first answers with 409 (\`already answered\`).
  - \`POST /answer\` (with edit key only): Updates answers on open rounds.
  - \`POST /my-answers\` (with edit key only): Retrieves saved answers.
  - Rejects any request carrying both an invitation token and an edit key with 400.
- **Anonymous Storage & Schema (\`0008_submissions.sql\`, \`0006_submission_index.sql\`)**:
  - \`submission\` and \`answer\` tables created \`WITHOUT ROWID\` with random 128-bit keys. Neither table stores person, invitation, or timestamp columns.
  - Deleting a person removes their \`participation\` records, but their anonymous \`submission\` and \`answer\` rows survive.
- **Rule-Based Comment Redaction (\`packages/domain/src/privacy/Redaction.ts\`)**:
  - Implements pure \`redact(text, roster)\` removing roster names, emails, URLs, @handles, and phone numbers before comments are stored in the database.
- **Oxlint Query Lint (A3)**:
  - Added \`privacy-query\` lint rule to \`tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat\` preventing \`rowid\`, joining anonymous with identified tables, and unordered \`SELECT *\`.
- **Test Suite**:
  - Invariants A1, A2, A4 (unlinkability harness across all 3 seeds), A8 (double submission rejection), and A9 (person deletion survival) in \`Submissions.privacy.test.ts\`.
  - Endpoint behavior and Invariant A5 (rejecting requests with both token and edit key) in \`SubmissionWorker.test.ts\`.
  - 11 redaction unit and property tests in \`Redaction.test.ts\`.

Closes #43

=== PR 63
R1 10: Answer page (static entry) (#44)
Closes #44

## Summary
Implements the static entry answer page (slice R1 10) according to ADR 0005, ADR 0007, ADR 0008, and ADR 0009:
- **Variant A Architecture**: Prerendered static HTML entry with minified inline CSS and a lean, plain TypeScript controller (no React, Preact, or Base UI).
- **Token Exchange & Isolation**: On load, extracts fragment `#t=<token>&v=<1-5>`, strips immediately with `history.replaceState`, and caches in `sessionStorage` until first save. Head bootstrap script kicks off token exchange (`POST /exchange`) before DOM parsing completes. Effect Schema validator is loaded dynamically after initial paint.
- **Screen 1**: First rating preselected from URL param `v`, anonymity statement placed prominently directly above 'Save and continue'. Zero network POSTs occur before member interaction.
- **First Save & Invariant A5**: Tapping 'Save and continue' or changing rating value generates a cryptographically random 256-bit Edit key stored in `localStorage` (`sb_edit_<roundId>`), confirms the first answer via `POST /first-answer`, and purges the invitation token from memory and `sessionStorage`. Subsequent requests carry only the Edit key.
- **Screen 2+**: Renders remaining questions one at a time on mobile and all on one page on desktop (`min-width: 640px`). Each answer and comment autosaves on change/blur.
- **Comments & Transparency**: Under comment textarea, displays the ADR 0009 disclosure notice and live feedback: `Your Lead will see: [redacted text]`.
- **States & Completion**: Thank-you screen displays up to 3 open Actions; graceful handling for already answered (409), other browser, closed rounds, and noscript alert.
- **Budgets & Performance**: Critical path JS <= 10 KB gzip, HTML <= 8 KB, inline CSS <= 2 KB.
- **CI Performance Gate**: Lighthouse CI gate script in `infra/scripts/lighthouse-gate.ts` enforcing FCP <= 800 ms, LCP <= 1.3 s, and TBT <= 50 ms.
- **Accessibility & Tests**: WCAG 2.2 AA compliant (44px targets, visible focus, semantic markup verified with `@axe-core/playwright`), unit budgets test, and Playwright scanner & unlinkability end-to-end tests.

=== PR 64
R1 11: Result computation and minimum group size rules (#45)
Resolves #45 (Slice 11 of Release 1: implementation).

## Summary
- **Domain Results Engine (`packages/domain/src/rounds/Results.ts`)**:
  - Computes Round Results with strict enforcement of minimum group size rules (R1–R11, ADR 0004).
  - Effective $N = \max(\text{stored } N, \text{current } N)$.
  - Checks $N$ per aggregate against its own Contributors.
  - Dimension scores use only Questions that meet $N$ individually (leaving out sub-$N$ questions to prevent subtraction-based recovery).
  - Distribution options (1–5) and single-choice counts have no per-option minimum when the question meets $N$.
  - Shuffled, unlinked comments shown only when total Round submissions $\ge N$.
  - 12-round trend calculation with gaps marked on sub-$N$ rounds.
  - Typical change calculations & highlights (Issue #4): $|\text{change}| \ge 2 \times \text{typicalChange}$ and $\ge 0.3$, with 6 usable rounds baseline warm-up note and matched question subset annotations for dimensions.
- **DO Storage & Migration (`packages/cloudflare`)**:
  - Added migration `0009_results.sql` creating `round_result` table (`WITHOUT ROWID`, `PRIMARY KEY (round_id)`).
  - Implemented `executeComputeJob` in `Organization.ts`, storing precomputed Results and moving state to ready and shared.
  - Added retries and operator alerting on repeated failures (`delayed: true`).
  - Added `viewResults` and `recomputeResult` methods on Organization DO with caller authorization (Lead sees comments, members see scores without comments, non-member admin denied).
- **Testing & Verification**:
  - `packages/domain/src/rounds/Results.test.ts`: R1–R11 rule table test cases, Issue #4 noise/highlight worked examples, warm-up baseline, dimension subsets.
  - `packages/domain/src/rounds/Results.privacy.test.ts`: Privacy invariants P1–P3 including property test over 50 generated rounds.
  - `packages/cloudflare/src/ResultsStorage.test.ts`: SQLite schema, cascade deletion, replacement in place, and 104-round (2 years) performance benchmark (< 50ms, well under 1.5s SLA).

I found 13 problems against the Release 1 spec. The most serious: the end-to-end flow SPEC §7 requires is still all placeholders, and the results path has three minimum-group-size defects. Commit range reviewed: `db3821af...HEAD`.

**(a) Missing or partial**

1. **End-to-end flow never built.** #48 asks for the Playwright flow "create a Pulse … create an Action". All seven steps in `infra/tests/e2e/flow.spec.ts:9-15` are still `test.fixme`.
2. **No property test runs over Result endpoints.** #48: "Any endpoint whose response contains Result data must be listed with an input generator". `rounds.getResults` has `inputs: Arbitrary.Constant({})` (`packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts:146`), and nothing reads `.inputs`.
3. **No API test on Result endpoints.** #46: "API tests that no endpoint returns an aggregate below N for any role". No adapter test calls `getResults`. The role check P4 (`Results.privacy.test.ts:248-250`) builds `{...result, comments: []}` itself and then asserts on it, so it proves nothing.
4. **A4 doesn't test the real write path.** It writes rows with its own SQL (`Submissions.privacy.test.ts:110-124`) instead of calling the real `recordFirstAnswer`.
5. **Canary sweep is incomplete.** #48 lists "Queue and DLQ messages, R2, D1, and response bodies" and A6. The sweep covers Workers Logs only (`canary-sweep.ts:12-13`), and A6 exists nowhere.
6. **Lead controls have no UI.** #42 asks for "failed Invitations with their reason and a **Resend** button", and #41 asks for skip, pause, close early and cancel. These exist only in the API. The app has no Rounds route or list (`apps/web/src/app/routes.ts`), so Results are reachable only from the results-ready email link.
7. **Dimensions show no sample size.** #46 asks for "per-Dimension scores, each with its Contributor count". `DimensionResult` has no count (`Results.ts:91-100`).
8. **Anonymity statement leaves out what the Lead sees.** SPEC §5.2 says the answer page states "what the lead will and will not see", with N as the example. The text is hard-coded as "Your name is never stored…" (`Organization.ts:435,618,1206`; `SqlRounds.ts:797`).

**(b) Scope creep**

- Nothing material. The `__test` routes only exist on `test_` stages (`EmailTestRoutes.ts:9`).

**(c) Looks implemented but wrong**

9. **Raw Invitation tokens stored.** #42: "token stored only as a hash". The plain token goes into `schedule_job.payload` for send and reminder jobs (`Organization.ts:449,470`).
10. **Raising N leaves trend scores visible.** ADR 0004 says effective N = max(stored, current). `enforceEffectiveNOnResult` hides `score`, `distribution` and `change`, but leaves each `trend` (whose last point is this Round's score) and `typicalChange` untouched (`Results.ts:858-866, 873-891`). A score now below N stays visible on the trend.
11. **Wrong sample size on dimension trends.** The trend table labels `usableQuestionCount` as "Contributors" (`apps/web/src/app/results.ts:159`). That is a count of Questions, not people.
12. **Weekly time zones only half work.** SPEC §5.1: "Monday 9:00 means 9:00 for each recipient". The open job is scheduled with the Team's time zone for every member (`Organization.ts:176,280`). Members whose own zone is ahead of the Team's get sent immediately at open, so late (`:442`).
13. **Links hard-coded to production.** `baseUrl` and `resultsUrl` are `https://app.surveybeat.app` (`Organization.ts:437,577`), so Invitations and results emails sent from staging or `pr-<n>` stages point at production.

**Confirmed OK:** Submissions have no Person or time column, and each first Answer is stored in one transaction. Comments are redacted before insert (`SqlRounds.ts:628,670`). Org admins can't view Results or Actions (`Permissions.ts:75,82`). Submission Worker observability is off. Actions appear in the next Invitation. Reminders follow the W−1 and 6-hour rules.
